This week you will measure **associations between variables** with correlation, handle **missing data points**, and take your first steps into **unsupervised learning** with clustering. Use the language toggle above to switch between R and Python.

<h3>Quiz 1: Correlation <span id="quiz-done-w3_q_correlation" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What is the main difference between Pearson and Spearman correlation?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cor1" id="cor1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="cor1a">They always return the exact same value</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cor1" id="cor1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="cor1b">Pearson measures the linear relationship using raw values; Spearman uses ranks to measure monotonic relationships</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cor1" id="cor1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="cor1c">Pearson only works on categorical variables</label></div>
    <div id="cor1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> What does <code>cor(dat$stab.glu, dat$glyhb, method='pearson')</code> compute?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cor2" id="cor2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="cor2a">The Pearson correlation coefficient between the two variables</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cor2" id="cor2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="cor2b">The p-value of a t-test comparing the two variables</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cor2" id="cor2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="cor2c">The mean difference between the two variables</label></div>
    <div id="cor2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> Why is Spearman correlation often more robust to outliers than Pearson?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cor3" id="cor3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="cor3a">It automatically removes missing values</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cor3" id="cor3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="cor3b">It is based on ranks rather than raw values, so extreme values shift the ranks only slightly</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cor3" id="cor3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="cor3c">It only works with normally distributed data</label></div>
    <div id="cor3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkCorrelationQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="correlation-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 2: Missing Data <span id="quiz-done-w3_q_missing" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> Given <code>rmv.rows &lt;- apply(dat, 1, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))</code>, what does <code>i.missing &lt;- which(rmv.rows &gt; 0)</code> contain?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="md1" id="md1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="md1a">The total number of missing values in the dataset</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="md1" id="md1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="md1b">The row indices of patients that have at least one missing value</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="md1" id="md1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="md1c">The column names that contain missing values</label></div>
    <div id="md1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> Why do we usually handle missing values before computing correlations or running k-means?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="md2" id="md2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="md2a">R cannot store <code>NA</code> in a dataframe at all</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="md2" id="md2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="md2b">Functions like <code>cor()</code> or <code>kmeans()</code> cannot handle <code>NA</code>s and will fail or return <code>NA</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="md2" id="md2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="md2c">Missing values always mean the whole row was measured incorrectly</label></div>
    <div id="md2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What does <code>dat[-i.missing, ]</code> do?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="md3" id="md3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="md3a">Keeps only the rows with missing values</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="md3" id="md3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="md3b">Removes the rows with missing values, keeping everyone else</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="md3" id="md3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="md3c">Removes the columns with missing values</label></div>
    <div id="md3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkMissingQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="missing-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 3: Introduction to Clustering <span id="quiz-done-w3_q_clustering" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What does "unsupervised" mean in unsupervised learning?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cl1" id="cl1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="cl1a">The analysis needs no data at all</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cl1" id="cl1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="cl1b">There are no known group labels — the method finds structure purely from the data itself</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cl1" id="cl1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="cl1c">A human manually assigns every observation to a group first</label></div>
    <div id="cl1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> What is the general goal of clustering?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cl2" id="cl2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="cl2a">Predict a continuous outcome variable from other variables</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cl2" id="cl2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="cl2b">Group similar observations together while separating the dissimilar ones</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cl2" id="cl2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="cl2c">Remove all missing values from a dataset</label></div>
    <div id="cl2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> In the gene expression example (<code>brca.exp</code>, genes × samples), what are we clustering when we run <code>kmeans(x = t(brca.exp), ...)</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cl3" id="cl3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="cl3a">The genes (rows)</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cl3" id="cl3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="cl3b">The samples/patients (columns) — that's why the matrix is transposed with <code>t()</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="cl3" id="cl3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="cl3c">The p-values of a statistical test</label></div>
    <div id="cl3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkClusteringQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="clustering-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 4: K-means Clustering <span id="quiz-done-w3_q_kmeans" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> In <code>kmeans(x, centers = k, nstart = 10)</code>, what does <code>centers</code> control?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="km1" id="km1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="km1a">The number of clusters requested</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="km1" id="km1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="km1b">The number of random restarts</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="km1" id="km1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="km1c">The distance metric used</label></div>
    <div id="km1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> What does the Within Sum of Squares (WSS, <code>km$tot.withinss</code>) measure?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="km2" id="km2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="km2a">How spread out the entire dataset is, regardless of clustering</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="km2" id="km2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="km2b">How compact each cluster is — lower WSS means tighter clusters</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="km2" id="km2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="km2c">The number of points assigned to each cluster</label></div>
    <div id="km2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> Why does WSS always decrease as you increase the number of clusters <code>k</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="km3" id="km3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="km3a">Because <code>kmeans()</code> recalculates the data randomly each time</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="km3" id="km3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="km3b">Because with more clusters, points sit closer to their own centroid — down to zero once every point is its own cluster</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="km3" id="km3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="km3c">Because R ignores clusters beyond <code>k = 5</code></label></div>
    <div id="km3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkKmeansQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="kmeans-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<h3>Quiz 5: Plenum Recap — Correlation &amp; Clustering Deep Dive <span id="quiz-done-w3_q_plenum" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> In the plenum, a single outlier point was added to a strong linear relationship and moved further and further away. What happened to the Pearson and Spearman correlations?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pl1" id="pl1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pl1a">Both stayed exactly the same</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pl1" id="pl1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pl1b">The Pearson correlation kept changing as the outlier moved further away, while the Spearman correlation stayed constant — because moving the point further doesn't change its rank</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pl1" id="pl1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pl1c">The Spearman correlation kept changing while Pearson stayed constant</label></div>
    <div id="pl1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> The plenum simulated points scattered randomly in a circle (no real cluster structure) and ran k-means with <code>centers = 2</code> 25 times with different random initializations. What did this demonstrate?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pl2" id="pl2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pl2a">K-means always converges to the exact same clustering, regardless of the data</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pl2" id="pl2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pl2b">When there is no real cluster structure in the data, the k-means result can differ a lot depending on the random initialization</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pl2" id="pl2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pl2c">K-means cannot be run more than once on the same dataset</label></div>
    <div id="pl2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> The plenum compared standard k-means (Euclidean distance) with a custom "k-medians" implementation using Manhattan distance on the same 6 points. What does this comparison illustrate?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pl3" id="pl3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pl3a">Manhattan and Euclidean distance always produce identical clusters</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pl3" id="pl3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pl3b">The choice of distance metric (and center type: mean vs. median) can change which points end up in which cluster</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pl3" id="pl3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pl3c">Manhattan distance can only be used for time-series data</label></div>
    <div id="pl3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkPlenumQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="plenum-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<h3 style="margin-top:0.5rem;">Quiz 1: Correlation <span style="font-size:0.8rem;color:#7c9cef;font-weight:normal;">(pandas equivalent of R cor())</span></h3>
